KEY: shuowen:10    ||    CHINESE: 示 — 天垂象，見吉凶，所以示人也。从二。(二，古文上字。)三垂，日月星也。觀乎天文，以察時變。示，神事也。凡示之屬皆从示。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: Heaven displays signs revealing good and ill fortune, thereby instructing people. Formed from 二 (the ancient form of 上). The three hanging strokes are the sun, moon and stars. Observing heavenly patterns reveals seasonal changes. 示 concerns divine affairs. All characters in the 示 category are formed from 示.

KEY: shuowen:41    ||    CHINESE: 祠 — 春祭曰祠。品物少，多文詞也。从示司聲。仲春之月，祠不用犧牲，用圭璧及皮幣。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: The spring sacrifice is called 祠: its offerings are few, but its ritual words many. KEY: shuowen:78    ||    CHINESE: 王 — 天下所歸往也。董仲舒曰：“古之造文者，三畫而連其中謂之王。三者，天、地、人也，而參通之者王也。”孔子曰：“一貫三爲王。”凡王之屬皆从王。[李陽冰曰：“中畫近上。王者，則天之義。”]    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: That to which all under heaven turn. Dong Zhongshu said: “The ancient makers of writing called three strokes joined through their middle 王. The three are heaven, earth and humanity; the king connects all three.” Confucius said: “One stroke running through three makes 王.” All characters in the 王 category are formed from 王. [Li Yangbing said: “The middle stroke is close to the upper one: the king models himself on Heaven.”]

KEY: shuowen:79    ||    CHINESE: 閏 — 餘分之月，五歲再閏，告朔之禮，天子居宗廟，閏月居門中。从王在門中。《周禮》曰：“閏月，王居門中，終月也。”    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: The month of the surplus fraction; there are two intercalations in five years. During the rite announcing the new moon, the Son of Heaven occupies the ancestral temple; in an intercalary month he occupies the gateway. Formed from 王 inside 門. The Rites of Zhou says: “In an intercalary month the king occupies the gateway throughout the month.”

KEY: shuowen:80    ||    CHINESE: 皇 — 大也。从自。自，始也。始皇者，三皇，大君也。自，讀若鼻，今俗以始生子爲鼻子。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: Great. Formed from 自. 自 means beginning. The earliest sovereigns were the Three Sovereigns, great rulers. 自 is pronounced like 鼻; common speech now calls the firstborn child 鼻子.

KEY: shuowen:81    ||    CHINESE: 玉 — 石之美。有五德：潤澤以溫，仁之方也；䚡理自外，可以知中，義之方也；其聲舒揚，尃以遠聞，智之方也；不橈而折，勇之方也；銳廉而不技，絜之方也。象三玉之連。\|，其貫也。凡玉之屬皆从玉。[陽冰曰：“三畫正均如貫玉也。”]    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: Beautiful stone. It has five virtues: warm moist luster embodies benevolence; its internal texture can be known from outside, embodying righteousness; its expansive, spreading sound is heard afar, embodying wisdom; breaking rather than bending embodies courage; sharp edges that do not injure embody purity. It depicts three linked pieces of jade; \| is their string. All characters in the 玉 category are formed from 玉. [Yangbing said: “The three strokes are evenly spaced, like strung jade.”]

KEY: shuowen:1417    ||    CHINESE: 疋 — 足也。上象腓腸，下从止。《弟子職》曰：“問疋何止。”古文以爲《詩·大疋》字。亦以爲足字。或曰胥字。一曰疋，記也。凡疋之屬皆从疋。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT [UNCERTAIN]: A foot. KEY: shuowen:1418    ||    CHINESE: 𤴙 — 門戶疏䆫也。从疋，疋亦聲。囪象𤴙形。讀若疏。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: An open lattice window in a doorway. Formed from 疋; 疋 also indicates the sound. 囪 depicts its form. Pronounced like 疏.

KEY: shuowen:1444    ||    CHINESE: 㐁 — 舌皃。从𧮫省。象形。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: The appearance of a tongue. Formed from abbreviated 𧮫; a pictograph.

KEY: shuowen:1754    ||    CHINESE: 𢍉 — 舉也。从廾甶聲。《春秋傳》曰：“晉人或以廣墜，楚人𢍉之。”黃顥說：廣車陷，楚人爲舉之。杜林以爲騏麟字。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: To lift. Formed from 廾, with 甶 indicating the sound. Du Lin takes it as a character for 騏麟.

KEY: shuowen:2347    ||    CHINESE: 羌 — 西戎牧羊人也。从人从羊，羊亦聲。南方蠻閩从虫，北方狄从犬，東方貉从豸，西方羌从羊：此六種也。西南僰人、僬僥，从人；蓋在坤地，頗有順理之性。唯東夷从大。大，人也。夷俗仁，仁者壽，有君子不死之國。孔子曰：“道不行，欲之九夷，乘桴浮於海。”有以也。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: Shepherds among the western Rong. Southwestern 僰 and 僬僥 contain 人: perhaps, occupying the kun quarter, they have a somewhat compliant nature. Only eastern 夷 contains 大; 大 means a person. Yi customs are benevolent; the benevolent live long, and there is a country of gentlemen who do not die. Confucius said: “The Way is not practiced; I wish to go to the Nine Yi, taking a raft to float on the sea.” There was a reason for this.

KEY: shuowen:2480    ||    CHINESE: 焉 — 焉鳥，黃色，出於江淮。象形。凡字：朋者，羽蟲之屬；烏者，日中之禽；舄者，知太歲之所在；燕者，請子之𠋫，作巢避戊己。所䝿者故皆象形。焉亦是也。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT [UNCERTAIN]: The yellow 焉 bird, found along the Yangtze and Huai. A pictograph. As for these graphs: 朋 belongs to feathered creatures; 烏 is the bird in the sun; 舄 knows the whereabouts of the Grand Year; 燕 marks the season for seeking offspring and builds nests avoiding wu and ji. Because these are esteemed, all are pictographs. 焉 is so too.

KEY: shuowen:4287    ||    CHINESE: 曐 — 萬物之精，上爲列星。从晶生聲。一曰象形。从口，古口復注中，故與日同。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: The essences of all things become the arrayed stars above. Formed from 晶, with 生 indicating the sound. Another explanation: pictographic, using 口; ancient 口 had a mark added inside, thus matching 日.

KEY: shuowen:4347    ||    CHINESE: 鼎 — 三足兩耳，和五味之寶器也。昔禹收九牧之金，鑄鼎荆山之下，入山林川澤，螭魅蝄蜽，莫能逢之，以協承天休。《易》卦：巽木於下者爲鼎，象析木以炊也。籒文以鼎爲貞字。凡鼎之屬皆从鼎。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: A precious vessel with three legs and two handles for blending the five flavors. In the Changes, Xun-wood below makes the 鼎 hexagram, depicting split wood for cooking. The large-seal script uses 鼎 for 貞. All characters in this group follow 鼎.

KEY: shuowen:4348    ||    CHINESE: 鼒 — 鼎之圜掩上者。从鼎才聲。《詩》曰：“鼐鼎及鼒。”    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: A tripod with a rounded, narrowed top. Formed from 鼎, with 才 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “鼐 tripods, 鼎 tripods and 鼒.”

Formed from 禾, with 爯 indicating the sound. Grain grows at the spring equinox. At the summer solstice the sun’s shadow can be measured. Grain has awns, which become fixed at the autumn equinox. In pitch-pipe measurement, twelve awns equal one fen; ten fen make one cun. By weight, twelve grains make one fen, and twelve fen one zhu. Thus all standards and measures follow 禾.

KEY: shuowen:5209    ||    CHINESE: 丘 — 土之高也，非人所爲也。从北从一。一，地也，人居在丘南，故从北。中邦之居，在崐崘東南。一曰四方高，中央下爲丘。象形。凡丘之屬皆从丘。(今隷變作丘。)    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: A natural rise of earth, not made by people. KEY: shuowen:5210    ||    CHINESE: 虛 — 大丘也。崐崘丘謂之崐崘虛。古者九夫爲井，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘。丘謂之虛。从丘虍聲。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: A great hill: Kunlun Hill is called Kunlun Xu. KEY: shuowen:5400    ||    CHINESE: 尺 — 十寸也。人手卻十分動脈爲寸口。十寸爲尺。尺，所以指尺䂓榘事也。从尸从乙。乙，所識也。周制，寸、尺、咫、尋、常、仞諸度量，皆以人之體爲法。凡尺之屬皆从尺。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT [UNCERTAIN]: Ten cun. On the human hand, the moving pulse ten divisions back forms the cun-opening; ten cun make one chi. Chi is used to indicate measures and regulate affairs. Formed from 尸 and 乙; 乙 is the marker. Under Zhou, cun, chi, zhi, xun, chang, ren and other measures all took the human body as their standard. All characters in this group follow 尺. The anatomical wording is uncertain.

KEY: shuowen:5402    ||    CHINESE: 尾 — 微也。从到毛在尸後。古人或飾系尾，西南夷亦然。凡尾之屬皆从尾。(今隸變作尾。)    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: Small or fine. Formed from inverted 毛 behind 尸. KEY: shuowen:5786    ||    CHINESE: 包 — 象人褢妊，巳在中，象子未成形也。元气起於子。子，人所生也。男左行三十，女右行二十，俱立於巳，爲夫婦。褢妊於巳，巳爲子，十月而生。男起巳至寅，女起巳至申。故男秊始寅，女秊始申也。凡包之屬皆从包。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: Depicts a pregnant person, with 巳 inside representing a child not yet fully formed. Primal qi begins at 子; a child is what people produce. The male moves leftward for thirty, the female rightward for twenty; both stand at 巳 and become husband and wife. Pregnancy begins at 巳; 巳 becomes 子, and birth occurs after ten months. The male starts at 巳 and reaches 寅; the female starts at 巳 and reaches 申. Hence male years begin at 寅, female years at 申. Formed from 𠃉 and 子. 𠃉 is the seasonal bird at whose arrival people pray for children. To obtain a child when it arrives is held auspicious and beautiful. KEY: shuowen:7665    ||    CHINESE: 乳 — 人及鳥生子曰乳，獸曰産。从孚从𠃉。𠃉者，玄鳥也。《明堂月令》：“玄鳥至之日，祠于高禖，以請子。”故乳从𠃉。請子必以𠃉至之日者，𠃉，春分來，秋分去，開生之候鳥，帝少昊司分之官也。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: For humans and birds, bearing young is called 乳; for beasts, 産. Formed from 孚 and 𠃉. 𠃉 is the dark bird. The Bright Hall's Monthly Ordinances says: 'On the day the dark bird arrives, sacrifice to the High Matchmaker to pray for children.' Thus 乳 includes 𠃉. Prayers for children must be on its arrival day because it comes at the spring equinox and leaves at the autumn equinox, a seasonal bird opening the time of birth, Emperor Shaohao's official in charge of the equinoxes.

KEY: shuowen:7666    ||    CHINESE: 不 — 鳥飛上翔不下來也。从一，一猶天也。象形。凡不之屬皆从不。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT: A bird flying upward and soaring without coming down. Formed from 一, which represents heaven; a pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 不.

All characters in this group are formed from 辰.

KEY: shuowen:9833    ||    CHINESE: 亥 — 荄也。十月，微陽起，接盛陰。从二，二，古文上字。一人男，一人女也。从乙，象褢子咳咳之形。《春秋傳》曰：“亥有二首六身。”凡亥之屬皆从亥。    ||    ENGLISH DRAFT [UNCERTAIN]: A root. In the tenth month faint yang arises and joins abundant yin. Formed from 二, ancient-script 上. One person is male and one female. Includes 乙, depicting carrying a child, with its condition described as 咳咳; the precise sense of 咳咳 is uncertain. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: '亥 has two heads and six bodies.' All characters in this group are formed from 亥.
